title: Microsoft Edge: security update alerts with a severity threshold in the Edge management service
notes: claim 62: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
the verifier wrote "hold" but listed no blocker and fewer than three majors; the claims decide, so the page is not held
summary: The briefing is held because its impact rationale says the Learn page does not mention end users, although that page describes user-facing restart actions. The rollout, unchanged notification default and access paths are supported; the rationale needs to distinguish security update alerts from the dashboard's separate update actions.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 558435 concerns Microsoft Edge security update alerts in the Edge management service.

claims.claim: Administrators can configure a minimum severity threshold, and new Edge updates generate alerts when their security fixes meet or exceed it.
claims.quote: You can configure a minimum severity threshold for security update alerts. Alerts are generated when a newly released Microsoft Edge update includes security fixes that meet or exceed the configured severity level, including zero-day vulnerability fixes.

claims.claim: The security fixes covered by the alerts include zero-day vulnerability fixes.
claims.quote: Alerts are generated when a newly released Microsoft Edge update includes security fixes that meet or exceed the configured severity level, including zero-day vulnerability fixes.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the aim as identifying updates needing attention while avoiding unnecessary notifications for routine releases.
claims.quote: This helps organizations quickly identify updates that may require attention, while avoiding unnecessary notifications for routine releases.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Enable version monitoring must be turned on to view device insights on the monitoring dashboard and receive the necessary diagnostic data.
claims.quote: To view device insights on this page, you must first turn on the toggle to Enable version monitoring. This is a mandatory step to ensure that Microsoft Edge receives the necessary diagnostic data

claims.claim: One version-monitoring option sends optional diagnostic data without page URL and per-page usage data.
claims.quote: Send optional diagnostic data without URL data: ... It also disables the UrlDiagnosticDataEnabled policy to not send data about page URLs and per-page usage.

claims.claim: The other version-monitoring option sends optional diagnostic data including page URL and per-page usage data.
claims.quote: Send optional diagnostic data with URL data: ... It also enables the UrlDiagnosticDataEnabled policy to send data about page URLs and per-page usage

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not separately specify whether generating security update alerts themselves requires Enable version monitoring.
claims.quote: Searched: Edge management service security update alerts Enable version monitoring. Read the full Monitoring dashboard page: the toggle is mandatory for device insights; Security update alerts does not separately state a prerequisite for generating the release alert itself.

claims.claim: Device update information is deleted from the Edge management service after the device has not sent data for 30 days.
claims.quote: If a device has not sent data for 30 days, then the update information for that device will be deleted from the Edge management service.

claims.claim: The monitoring page documents Force auto restart when device is idle as an administrator-selected update action.
claims.quote: For devices that are out of date, you can choose one of the following actions ... Force auto restart when device is idle: This action automatically restarts the users' browsers to apply the latest update when their device is detected as idle.

claims.claim: Force auto restart when device is idle can cause loss of content input.
claims.quote: Force auto restart when device is idle: ... Note: This may cause loss of content input.

claims.claim: Recommend restart is another documented update action on the monitoring page.
claims.quote: Recommend restart: This action sends a notification to the user to restart their browser to apply the latest update.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The sources do not document an alert automatically updating devices or triggering either restart action.
claims.quote: Searched: Edge security update alerts monitoring automatically email. Read Monitoring dashboard, including Edge update status and Security update alerts, plus MC1458480. Actions are described as administrator choices, not automatic consequences of generating an alert.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not document email, another delivery channel, or recipient selection for these security update alerts.
claims.quote: Searched: Edge management service security update alerts email notifications recipients; security update alerts monitoring automatically email. Read Monitoring dashboard and Edge release-note excerpts; email results concerned extension requests or other products, not these alerts.

claims.claim: Setting EdgeManagementEnabled to 0 or disabled stops browsers checking in with the Edge management service.

claims.fix: Remove controls[2] and its rendered table row, retaining the supported EdgeManagementEnabled explanation already in the Governance controls prose. The policy instruction is true, but it is not a runnable API or automation call as the table and standard require; do not replace it with a false undocumented-automation claim.

claims.claim: EdgeManagementEnabled controls browser connections to the management service to download and apply assigned policies.
claims.quote: If you enable or don't configure this policy, Microsoft Edge attempts to connect to the Microsoft Edge management service to download and apply policy assigned to the Azure AD account of the user.

claims.claim: EdgeManagementEnabled is supported on Windows, while its policy page lists macOS, Android and iOS as not supported.
claims.quote: Windows: ≥ 115; macOS: Not supported; Android: Not supported; iOS: Not supported

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed whether EdgeManagementEnabled governs monitoring data or security update alerts.
claims.quote: Searched: EdgeManagementEnabled monitoring alerts; Microsoft Graph Edge management service access API security update alerts EdgeManagementEnabled monitoring. Read EdgeManagementEnabled, Monitoring dashboard and service guide; none connects this policy to alert generation or monitoring collection.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not state a user licence requirement for a device to be counted in monitoring.
claims.quote: Searched: Edge management service license monitoring; Microsoft Edge management service security update alerts licensing pricing billing meter license monitoring dashboard. Read Monitoring dashboard and the service prerequisites; no user licence requirement for device counting found.

claims.claim: Edge handles untrusted content on every managed device.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge browser untrusted web content installed every managed device security updates risk. Read Monitoring dashboard and Microsoft Edge security for your business excerpts; neither establishes that Edge handles content on every managed device.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'Browser sessions without the latest security updates might be at risk.' This is stated on the already-cited Monitoring dashboard page.

claims.claim: The alerts described in the briefing are presented to administrators using the Edge management service.
claims.quote: Administrators can now choose a severity threshold and receive alerts when a new Edge update includes security fixes that meet or exceed that threshold, including zero-day fixes.

claims.claim: End users are not mentioned in the roadmap item, the Message Center post or the Learn page.
claims.quote: Recommend restart: This action sends a notification to the user to restart their browser to apply the latest update. No action will be taken on their behalf, and users may choose whether to act upon the notification.
claims.fix: Replace the impact rationale with: 'Low. Microsoft describes security update alerts as an administrator capability displayed in the monitoring dashboard.' The Learn page does mention end users for separate restart actions; this does not establish that alerts automatically trigger those actions.
